diagram_math_checks.objects: Coarse Coxeter cell C_S and its proper spherical-coset boundary
diagram_math_checks.checks: Six distinct vertices represent singleton cosets at 1,s,st,sts,ts,t. Independently checked in S3 with s=(12), t=(23): right multiplication along the boundary is s,t,s,t,s,t, returning t*t=1. Thus each boundary segment is wW_{s} or wW_{t}, with three edges of each type and degree 2 at every boundary vertex. Six boundary edges enclose exactly one coarse 2-cell; no radial subdivision is drawn.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Regular planar hexagon conditional on d_s=d_t
diagram_math_checks.local_basis: Statement (ii) and proof 1.2: six orbit angles spaced by pi/3.
diagram_math_checks.checks: Coordinates (0,1.5),(1.299038,.75),(1.299038,-.75),(0,-1.5),(-1.299038,-.75),(-1.299038,.75) approximate a regular hexagon, with independently computed side lengths 1.49999991,1.5,1.49999991,1.49999991,1.5,1.49999991. Caption explicitly retains d_s=d_t.

Four vertices are the four spherical subsets. The square boundary represents the four strict inclusions emptyset<{s}, {s}<S, S>{t}, {t}>emptyset. The diagonal is the comparable pair emptyset<S. It gives exactly the maximal chains emptyset<{s}<S and emptyset<{t}<S, whose triangles share the diagonal; no edge {s}--{t} is drawn. These are simplicial edges, not directional arrows. Caption distinguishes this chamber from the coarse Coxeter cell.
